extracted.intended_audience: aspiring fiction writers or first-time novella writers
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, step-by-step guidance for planning, writing, revising, and preparing a novella (short fiction ~20k–40k words) aimed at writers wanting to learn or complete this specific short-form book-length fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novella length and defining characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical word count ~20,000–40,000 words (no more than ~200 pages); sits between short story and novel; typically simplistic, fast-paced, and symbolic; encourages readers to think about a central question or theme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given (Kafka's The Metamorphosis ~21k; Joyce Carol Oates's Black Water ~40k). Emphasizes that more than length, certain characteristics (pace, symbolism, thematic focus) make a piece a novella.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central question or thematic focus
rubrics_metrics.description: The novella should encourage the reader to think deeply about a central question or theme rather than disperse attention across many themes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use symbolism and focused plot/character development to explore the central question; the form's brevity favors depth on one or two ideas rather than many.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot complexity and narrative focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Novellas usually rely on a simpler plot—one or two key ideas or conflicts—focused primarily on a single character’s development rather than multiple interweaving storylines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit side plots and extensive backstories; avoid the kind of multi-threaded plotting common to novels. Novellas often do not use many chapters and instead maintain a tighter arc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pacing and delivering early momentum
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a faster pace than a typical novel; reach the first major conflict quickly and sustain momentum throughout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider starting in medias res to hook readers. In revision, delete repetitive background or behaviors, look for slow sections to tighten, and add suspense or foreshadowing where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of symbolism and figurative language
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ imagery, motifs, and figurative language (metaphor, simile, personification, hyperbole) to deepen themes and character in the limited space of a novella.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance is key: ensure literary techniques strengthen the story rather than distract. Symbolism in novellas can be dense and may reward re-reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outline key scenes and story mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: Create an outline mapping the central conflict, protagonist’s biggest problem, the solution/problems' resolution, and the sequence of critical scenes with settings, participants, and outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work through the entire arc before drafting so each scene advances the plot; note which scenes are exposition, rising action, turning point/climax, and resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point of view selection and consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose the narration POV (first, second, third) that best serves the story and remain consistent in that choice throughout the novella.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First person creates intimacy; second person is rare but can be effective; third person offers broader access to characters. Stick to the chosen POV to avoid reader confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character arc and protagonist development
rubrics_metrics.description: Design a believable emotional journey for the protagonist—decide what they will learn or how they will change (triumph, loss, discovery, etc.) and build motivations, decisions, and reactions accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop the main character in more depth than supporting characters; use emotions, motivations, and choices to make the transformation credible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding complicated subplots and extraneous elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Resist introducing tangential subplots, side characters, recurring flashbacks, or tedious dialogue that do not support the main storytelling thrust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask whether each character or event serves exposition, rising action, climax, or resolution. Remove or streamline anything that slows pace or distracts from the central conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show vs. tell: strategic use of figurative and literal language
rubrics_metrics.description: Know when to move the story with straightforward description and when to 'show' with imagery and figurative language to create vividness without stalling the plot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the draft is overly expository ('telling'), look for opportunities to show through action, dialogue, or imagery; iterate across drafts to ensure literary choices enhance, not hinder, pace or clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision process and seeking feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: After finishing a draft, allow time for revision and obtain feedback from trusted readers or editors to identify strengths and weaknesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide reviewers with a focused checklist (strong opening/closing, character development, setting, plot conflicts, dialogue, tone, diction, consistent verb tenses). Be open to constructive criticism and use it to produce subsequent drafts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading widely in the form
rubrics_metrics.description: Before and during writing, read many novellas across types and genres to study narrative and stylistic choices, structure, pacing, and voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze novellas you admire to discover category conventions and possibilities; examples cited include Animal Farm, Breakfast at Tiffany’s, A Christmas Carol, Of Mice and Men, The Old Man and the Sea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type-specific expectations (literary, inspirational, genre)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize different novella types: literary (psychological depth, challenging language), inspirational (shorter, emotionally driven), and genre (e.g., horror, sci‑fi, romance with specific tropes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor language, pacing, and scene choice to type: literary may use denser language and symbolism; inspirational aims for emotional resonance; genre novellas adhere to genre expectations and tropes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing for publication and format/design choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide how to present the finished novella as a trade book (self-publishing or professional tools), selecting book size, paper, cover type, and layout appropriate for the novella length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggestions include using Blurb’s BookWright or professional tools like Adobe InDesign or PDF uploaders; consider distribution options (sell online, share with friends, or distribute widely). Self-publishing is presented as a practical option for novellas.
